key_insight: Stable, physically useful elastic-turbulence simulations can be obtained even when the conformation tensor temporarily loses positive-definiteness, as long as resolution is above a minimum stability threshold.
engineering_relevance: This could reduce the computational cost of direct numerical simulation for polymeric flows, making high-fidelity studies of elastic turbulence more accessible.
method: Simulate dilute polymer flow in a low-Re plane channel with a conformation-tensor model.
Scan numerical resolution to identify two thresholds: blow-up at low resolution and positive-definite recovery at high resolution.
Compare statistics from intermediate-resolution runs against fully positive-definite simulations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that intermediate stable chaotic runs with local Tr(c)<3 violations still match mid-plane statistics of velocity, velocity gradients, and polymer stretch from positive-definite simulations.
watch_item: Local loss of positive-definiteness may still be unacceptable for quantities outside the reported mid-plane statistics, so validation is needed before using this shortcut broadly.
paper_title: No need to stay positive: a practical approach to direct numerical simulations of elastic turbulence
